newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -Euromark vol slips after steady Buba.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -Euromark vol slips after steady Buba.

text.p: Implied volatility of Euromark options on LIFFE drifted lower on Thursday with traders expecting the softer tone to persist for the next few weeks as the Bundesbank enters its summer recess.
"Volatility has come off a bit this morning, but there haven't been that many trades in Euromark," said one salesman, noting the contract had been heavily traded on Wednesday.
The Bundesbank held its last council meeting on Thursday ahead of a four week summer recess, leaving its discount, lombard and repo rates unchanged.
There had been some speculation the German central bank may move to variable-rate repos or make some kind of forex statement to give a filip to the weak mark.
The salesman said with the market spotlight away from German interest rate changes for the summer, Euromark volatility would likely be a bit softer in August.
"Volatility will probably drift a bit lower, but I wouldn't be caught on the short side going into the end of August," he said.
"There is a lot of talk about the possibility of a change in the repo rate in August."
Traders said September volatility levels were indicated around 8/11 percent, down from around 10.1/12.1 at Wednesday's close.

By 1430 GMT, December Euromarks were down seven basis points at 96.54, while September was down 0.04 at 96.72. Over 6,800 contracts had been traded in the 96.50 September put and 2,800 in the 97.00 September call.
